segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Hi everyone, welcome to the Snow Centre.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: My name’s Annie.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I hope you enjoyed the bus trip from the airport – we’ve certainly got plenty of snow today!

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Well, you’ve come to New Zealand’s premier snow and ski centre, and we’ve a whole load of activities for you during your week here.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Most visitors come here for the cross-country skiing, where you’re on fairly flat ground for most of the time, rather than going down steep mountainsides.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There are marked trails, but you can also leave these and go off on your own and that’s an experience not to be missed.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You can go at your own speed – it’s great aerobic exercise if you really push yourself, or if you prefer you can just glide gently along and enjoy the beautiful scenery.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This afternoon, you’ll be going on a dog-sled trip.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You may have seen our dogs on TV recently racing in the winter sled festival.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: If you want, you can have your own team for the afternoon and learn how to drive them, following behind our leader on the trail.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Or if you’d prefer, you can just sit back in the sled and enjoy the ride as a passenger.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: At the weekend, we have the team relay event, and you’re all welcome to join in.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We have a local school coming along, and a lot of the teachers are taking part too.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Participation rather than winning is the main focus, and there’s a medal for everyone who takes part.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Participants are in teams of two to four, and each team must complete four laps of the course.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: For your final expedition, you’ll head off to Mount Frenner wearing a pair of special snow shoes which allow you to walk on top of the snow.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This is an area where miners once searched for gold, though there are very few traces of their work left now.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: When the snow melts in summer, the mountain slopes are carpeted in flowers and plants.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It’s a long ascent, though not too steep, and walkers generally take a couple of days to get to the summit and return.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You’ll spend the night in our hut half-way up the mountain.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: That’s included in your package for the stay.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It’s got cooking facilities, firewood and water for drinking.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: For washing, we recommend you use melted snow, though, to conserve supplies.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We can take your luggage up on our snowmobile for you for just ten dollars a person.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The hut has cooking facilities so you can make a hot meal in the evening and morning, but you need to take your own food.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The weather on Mount Frenner can be very stormy.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In that case, stay in the hut – generally the storms don’t last long.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Don’t stress about getting back here to the centre in time to catch the airport bus – they’ll probably not be running anyway.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We do have an emergency locator beacon in the hut but only use that if it’s real emergency, like if someone’s ill or injured. —————– Now, let me tell you something about the different ski trails you can follow during your stay here.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Highland Trail’s directly accessible from where we are now.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This trail’s been designed to give first-timers an experience they’ll enjoy regardless of their age or skill, but it’s also ideal for experts to practise their technique.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Then there’s Pine Trail ... if you’re nervous about skiing, leave this one to the experts!

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You follow a steep valley looking right down on the river below – scary!

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But if you’ve fully mastered the techniques needed for hills, it’s great fun.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Stony Trail’s a good choice once you’ve got a general idea of the basics.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There are one or two tricky sections, but nothing too challenging.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There’s a shelter half-way where you can sit and take a break and enjoy the afternoon sunshine. And finally, Loser’s Trail.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This starts off following a gentle river valley but the last part is quite exposed so the snow conditions can be challenging – if it’s snowing or windy, check with us before you set out to make sure the trail’s open that day. Right, so now if you’d like to follow me, we’ll get started...

instructions: Complete the original Cambridge IELTS listening questions below.
questions.source_text:
SECTION 2
Questions 11-20
THE SNOW CENTRE
Choose the correct letter A, B or C.
Questions:
    Q Num: 11
    Text: Annie recommends that when cross-country skiing, the visitors should
    Options:
        get away from the regular trails.
        stop to enjoy views of the scenery.
        go at a slow speed at the beginning.
    Q Num: 12
    Text: What does Annie tell the group about this afternoon's dog-sled trip?
    Options:
        Those who want to can take part in a race.
        Anyone has the chance to drive a team of dogs.
        One group member will be chosen to lead the trail.
    Q Num: 13
    Text: What does Annie say about the team relay event?
    Options:
        All participants receive a medal.
        The course is 4 km long.
        Each team is led by a teacher.
    Q Num: 14
    Text: On the snow-shoe trip, the visitors will
    Options:
        visit an old gold mine.
        learn about unusual flowers.
        climb to the top of a mountain.
    Q Num: 15
    Text: The cost of accommodation in the mountain hut includes
    Options:
        a supply of drinking water.
        transport of visitors' luggage.
        cooked meals.
    Q Num: 16
    Text: If there is a storm while the visitors are in the hut, they should
    Options:
        contact the bus driver.
        wait until the weather improves.
        use the emergency locator beacon.
Mountain trails
What information does Annie give about skiing on each of the following mountain trails?
Choose FOUR answers from the box and write the correct letter A–F next to questions 17–20.

    Text: Highland Trail

    Q Num: 20
    Text: Loser's Trail

    Id: D
